title: Reduce CPU-side handshake latency with KV prefetching and burst scheduler
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed repeated CPU-side stalls on the request hot path under mixed workloads (short chat completions vs long generation). Root causes identified: 1) synchronous KV cache lookups and repeated syscall boundaries when requests hit cold prefixes; 2) aggressive thread-to-core pinning causing poor work-stealing and imbalanced queues during bursty traffic; 3) small, eager batching stalls while waiting for a strict batch size.

This PR introduces three coordinated runtime changes aimed at reducing per-request CPU latency and increasing sustained throughput without changing model kernels: 1) lightweight per-worker KV prefetch that issues asynchronous read-ahead for likely KV keys for requests in the ready queue (uses existing cache backend interface; prefetch is best-effort and does not change correctness); 2) a "burst scheduler" that allows short-lived requests to bypass strict batch-size gating and create micro-batches while longer requests are routed to slower path or cooperative workers; 3) relaxed thread affinity: we convert hard O(1) thread-to-core pinning in the CPU workerpool to soft affinity hints and enable work stealing across neighbouring NUMA domains when local queues exceed threshold.

Implementation notes: all changes are opt-in via runtime config flags under "runtime.experimental": kv_prefetch=true, burst_scheduler=enabled, soft_affinity=true. Prefetch is implemented as a non-blocking task scheduled on the worker's I/O executor and returns a lightweight future; if the prefetch misses or is in-flight, the request continues using the original lookup path so no correctness regressions. The scheduler change leverages the existing request classification pipeline (light vs heavy heuristics by token-budget and model-profile) to route to either micro-batcher or standard continuous-batcher. Micro-batches have a small token/time budget (configurable) and are flushed sooner to reduce latency tail.

Performance: on our internal chat workload (50% short completions, 50% long continuations) with 8 x A100 nodes: - median CPU request latency reduced 14% on p95 across hosts; - end-to-end throughput improved 11% measured at same p95 latency target; - KV cache hit-rate on first lookup improved ~6% due to prefetch, reducing remote reads. When soft_affinity=false and prefetch enabled, we saw no improvements—this confirms the scheduler+affinity changes are synergistic. Microbenchmarks attached in CI artifacts show the prefetch path adds ~120ns overhead on hot-path enqueues when miss rate is low.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for prefetch logic and scheduler were added. Integration tests simulate bursts and confirm no deadlocks or resource leaks. Canary rollout plan: enable flags on a small Dedicated pool, monitor CPU p95, KV remote-read rate, dispatcher queue lengths and revert if observations exceed thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: internal RFC linked in Linear ENG-12892
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks and perf regression guardrails
- [x] Opt-in flags behind runtime config
- [x] Observability hooks: new metrics (kv_prefetch.requests, kv_prefetch.hits, scheduler.microbatch.count)

Notes: this PR purposefully avoids kernel-level changes (no model operator modifications) to keep the blast radius small. Future follow-ups: adaptive prefetch heuristics based on prefix reuse rates; expose micro-batch budgeting in the console for fine-grained tuning.
commits: feat(prefetch): add per-worker kv prefetch task with non-blocking lookup
feat(scheduler): implement burst scheduler and micro-batching path
perf(workerpool): convert hard affinity pins to soft affinity hints and enable stealing
test: add integration tests for burst scenarios and prefetch correctness
docs: runtime flags and observability metric docs
discussion: Marco Ruiz: Can we make prefetch opt-out per-tenant? Some enterprise customers prefer strict I/O determinism.
Aisha Patel: Yes, added runtime flag and per-tenant override in config; default off for Private until validated.
Emily Chen: Concerned about extra memory pressure from in-flight prefetches under very high concurrency.
Aisha Patel: Prefetch is gated by a concurrency cap per-worker and global in-flight metric; added tests for cap enforcement.
Jared O'Neill: The soft affinity change worries me for NUMA heavy workloads — any regressions seen there?
Aisha Patel: We added NUMA-aware stealing thresholds and a stress test; performance on our NUMA synthetic was flat to +3%.
Marco Ruiz: Approved after CI green and perf numbers validated on canary.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in KV prefetch and burst scheduler to reduce CPU-side latency and improve throughput for mixed short/long workloads; disabled by default for Private installs. Observability: kv_prefetch.* and scheduler.microbatch.* metrics added.
notes: Canary metrics are stored under perf/canaries/2025-10-kv-prefetch; recommend 72h canary window before broader rollout.
